reconstruction.summary: For arbitrary finite real square matrices K(s,b) of width D, and arbitrary left/right real vectors, construct a dependent chain of N=n+1 binary cores with scalar boundary ranks. For each recursive binary word x=(b0,...,b(N-1)), its scalar contraction is left^T K(start,b0) K(start+1,b1) ... K(start+N-1,b(N-1)) right. All dimensions including D=0 are allowed. No normalization, rank, orthogonality, positivity, boundedness or invertibility premise is imposed. The construction and storage theorem concern exact algebraic tensor-chain objects, not circuits or runtime.

ambient_definitions.Core(l,r): Matrix (Fin l) (Fin 2 × Fin r) Real; entries A(a,(bit,b)) have old bond as row and bit/new bond as column.
ambient_definitions.Chain(n,l,r): Dependent inductive chain. nil(r):Chain(0,r,r); cons(A:Core(l,m),C:Chain(n,m,r)):Chain(n+1,l,r). The intermediate rank m is an index, not a padded physical register.
ambient_definitions.Word(n): Word(0)=Unit; Word(n+1)=Fin 2 × Word(n). The outermost bit is emitted by the first core. No integer endianness is specified by this module.
ambient_definitions.contract: contract(nil(r),x)=identity matrix on Fin r; contract(cons(A,C),(bit,y))=slice(A,bit)*contract(C,y). Thus matrix multiplication is left-to-right chronological, even though recursive evaluation of readout computes the suffix first.
ambient_definitions.maxBond: maxBond(nil(r))=r; maxBond(cons(A:Core(l,m),C))=max(l,maxBond(C)). Includes both boundary dimensions and every actual internal rank.

reconstruction.inventory_method: Counted public top-level abbrev/def/theorem declarations from the entire actual module, then checked each in the freshly elaborated complete source. There are 13: 6 definition/abbreviation declarations and 7 theorems. Exact elaborated types and axiom prints are retained in decoder-lean-log.json.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.Kernel
public_declarations.signature: Kernel (D : Nat) := Nat → Fin 2 → Matrix (Fin D) (Fin D) Real
public_declarations.meaning: An arbitrary position/bit-indexed real D-by-D matrix family defined at all natural positions; no access or evaluation cost is attached.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.readout
public_declarations.signature: readout {D : Nat} (K : Kernel D) (right : Fin D → Real) (start : Nat) : {n : Nat} → Word n → Fin D → Real
public_declarations.binders: Implicit D and length n; explicit K,right,start,word,bond label. No logical premises.
public_declarations.meaning: For zero length returns right without reading K. For x=(bit,y), returns K(start,bit).mulVec(readout(K,right,start+1,y)). No left boundary is included.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.tailChain
public_declarations.signature: tailChain {D : Nat} (K : Kernel D) (right : Fin D → Real) (start n : Nat) : Chain (n+1) D 1
public_declarations.binders: Implicit D; explicit K,right,start,n. No logical premises.
public_declarations.meaning: Always nonempty. At n=0 the only core A(a,(bit,0))=(K(start,bit)*right)(a). For n>0 the first core is K(start,bit)(a,b), followed by the recursive chain starting at start+1. Original internal bonds are D, terminal bond is 1.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.tailChain_contract
public_declarations.signature: tailChain_contract {D : Nat} (K : Kernel D) (right : Fin D → Real) (start n : Nat) (x : Word (n+1)) (a : Fin D) : contract (tailChain K right start n) x a 0 = readout K right start x a
public_declarations.binders: Only dimensional, matrix, boundary, position, word and initial-label data. No extra proof bundle.
public_declarations.meaning: For each word and initial label, terminal-boundary absorption preserves the exact suffix contraction. D=0 makes the a binder uninhabited, rather than requiring a positive-rank premise.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.closeLeft
public_declarations.signature: closeLeft {n D : Nat} (left : Fin D → Real) : Chain (n+1) D 1 → Chain (n+1) 1 1
public_declarations.binders: Implicit n,D; explicit left and chain. No logical premises.
public_declarations.meaning: For cons(A,C), replace only the first core by A'(0,out)=sum_a left(a)*A(a,out), preserving C and all its ranks. Requires nonempty length by type, not a runtime test.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.closeLeft_contract
public_declarations.signature: closeLeft_contract {n D : Nat} (left : Fin D → Real) (C : Chain (n+1) D 1) (x : Word (n+1)) : contract (closeLeft left C) x 0 0 = sum_a left a * contract C x a 0
public_declarations.meaning: The first-core absorption implements the left bilinear boundary exactly; finite sums can be exchanged.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.ofKernel
public_declarations.signature: ofKernel {D : Nat} (K : Kernel D) (left right : Fin D → Real) (start n : Nat) : Chain (n+1) 1 1
public_declarations.binders: Implicit D; explicit K,left,right,start,n. No logical premises.
public_declarations.meaning: Literal composition closeLeft(left,tailChain(K,right,start,n)); it is not a choice-based factorization or dense-state decomposition. N=n+1, not n.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.ofKernel_contract
public_declarations.signature: ofKernel_contract {D : Nat} (K : Kernel D) (left right : Fin D → Real) (start n : Nat) (x : Word (n+1)) : contract (ofKernel K left right start n) x 0 0 = sum_a left a * readout K right start x a
public_declarations.meaning: Combines both absorption identities; the coefficient equals the ordered matrix product between explicit boundaries for every word.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.tailChain_maxBond
public_declarations.signature: tailChain_maxBond {D : Nat} (K : Kernel D) (right : Fin D → Real) (start n : Nat) : maxBond (tailChain K right start n) ≤ max D 1
public_declarations.meaning: Bounds dimensions, not matrix rank. Terminal rank 1 must remain in the bound even at D=0.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.ofKernel_maxBond
public_declarations.signature: ofKernel_maxBond {D : Nat} (K : Kernel D) (left right : Fin D → Real) (start n : Nat) : maxBond (ofKernel K left right start n) ≤ max D 1
public_declarations.meaning: Scalar boundaries and width-D internal bonds give this uniform bound. At N=1 there is no surviving D bond and maxBond is exactly 1.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.storedScalars
public_declarations.signature: storedScalars : {n l r : Nat} → Chain n l r → Nat
public_declarations.binders: Implicit n,l,r; explicit C. No proof premise.
public_declarations.meaning: nil contributes 0; each cons with core shape l by (2*m) contributes 2*l*m plus tail count, irrespective of numerical zeros, reuse or sparsity. It counts hypothetical dense local scalar addresses, not allocation or evaluation behavior of function-valued matrices.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.storedScalars_le
public_declarations.signature: storedScalars_le {n l r : Nat} (C : Chain n l r) (D : Nat) (h : maxBond C ≤ D) : storedScalars C ≤ 2*n*D^2
public_declarations.binders: Implicit n,l,r; explicit C and independent bound D; sole logical premise h:maxBond(C)≤D. D here is any maximum-bond cap, not necessarily a Kernel width.
public_declarations.meaning: Every core contributes at most 2*D^2. The maxBond premise includes both its left and right dimensions. For empty chains the count is 0 even if the carried boundary is nonzero; h still requires that boundary≤D.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.MatrixProductChain.ofKernel_storedScalars
public_declarations.signature: ofKernel_storedScalars {D : Nat} (K : Kernel D) (left right : Fin D → Real) (start n : Nat) : storedScalars (ofKernel K left right start n) ≤ 2*(n+1)*(max D 1)^2
public_declarations.binders: Only D,K,left,right,start,n. No logical premise; the maxBond fact is supplied inside the proof.
public_declarations.meaning: Specializes the generic dense-local-core address bound. It does not bound real arithmetic, obtaining K entries, finite-bit storage, preprocessing time, gates or quantum queries.

reconstruction.definition_audit: All six public definitions/abbreviations are literal type abbreviations or recursive/composed formulas. No characterized or quotient representative is chosen. noncomputable is consistent with exact Real algebra and is neither an efficiency theorem nor an impossibility theorem.
reconstruction.binder_audit: The only public logical premise is h:maxBond(C)≤D in storedScalars_le. Other binders are unconstrained data or typed dimensions/words/labels. Source-relative SOURCE/STANDING/TYPING/RULED/EXCESS classifications are deliberately not assigned in this blind pass.
reconstruction.proof_structure_from_actual_lean: tailChain_contract is an induction on n; closeLeft_contract distributes finite sums and swaps sum order; ofKernel_contract combines those identities. tailChain_maxBond is an induction; ofKernel_maxBond separates the one-core case. storedScalars_le is induction on C using both endpoint dimension bounds; ofKernel_storedScalars applies it with max D 1. This describes implementation topology only, not any withheld source construction topology.
reconstruction.resource_model: Exact dense local scalar-address count. For N=1, the closed chain has a 1-by-(2*1) core and exactly 2 scalar addresses for every original D. For N≥2, actual shapes are first 1→D, N-2 middle D→D, last D→1, giving 4*D+2*(N-2)*D^2 addresses. The theorem supplies the looser uniform bound 2*N*(max(D,1))^2. The sharper expression is explanatory; Lean probes certify its N=2 and N=3 cases only.
reconstruction.boundary_cases: readout accepts empty words and returns right; tailChain/ofKernel/closeLeft have no zero-length interface. D=0 is accepted: closed coefficients are zero. N=1 still stores two addresses and has maxBond=1. N≥2 with D=0 has zero local scalar addresses despite scalar endpoints. Zero/negative/non-normalized coefficients are allowed; no positivity or normalization is inferred.
